note: STP-708 - the exact surface of the published package.
Both lists below are compared as SETS, in BOTH directions: nothing missing
and nothing unexpected, with the difference named either way. A check that
only looks for what it expects is the same defect as a coverage gate that
counts instead of enumerating - it can be right about what you were looking
for and wrong about the rest.
That is not hypothetical. While this workflow was being written, the
concurrent npm-workspaces conversion silently changed what npm packs for a
member package: websockets-plugin went from 28 files to 10, losing all 18
docs, because with no 'files' array npm packlist fell back to ignore rules
and the root .gitignore's root-anchored /docs began reaching workspace
members at pack time. Every check stayed green. The first fix then restored
the docs and silently dropped CHANGELOG.md, which npm had been including by
default; 'did the docs come back?' passed, and only a full file-count
comparison caught it.
This root package declares 'files', so it is not exposed to that specific
fallback - but an SBOM built from a tarball inherits whatever the tarball
got wrong. Pack-based scoping fixes workspace enumeration; it does not make
the pack itself trustworthy. Only this list does.
CHANGING EITHER LIST IS A DELIBERATE ACT. If a release fails here, the
question is what changed the published surface, not how to relax the
threshold. Update these lists in the same change that alters the surface,
so it is visible in review.
packedFiles: verified 2026-09-09 against the tarball npm serves for
sketch-thru-plan-sdk@0.6.14 ('npm pack sketch-thru-plan-sdk@0.6.14'),
not merely against a local build. Paths are relative to the 'package/'
root that every npm tarball uses.
sbomComponents: package coordinates only, deliberately WITHOUT versions.
A package appearing or disappearing is a supply-chain change and stops the
release; a version moving inside an existing range is routine and is
covered by the vulnerability scan instead.
